purpose: Planning importance for reliable native rendering and eventual complete rendering replacement. These are initial engineering judgments, based on documented impact, breadth and safety/release consequences; not measured runtime frequency, a discovered dependency graph or effort estimates.

rubric.5: Critical: session correctness/safety, fundamental ownership, unresolved full-replacement boundaries or essential release acceptance.
rubric.4: High: visible scene fidelity, core capability, broad residual scope or a focused correctness investigation.
rubric.3: Medium: a bounded visual feature, optimization or independent bounded assurance.
rubric.2: Low: focused observation, fixtures or profiling with indirect player impact.
rubric.1: Supporting: narrow diagnostic/research work without an identified current correctness blocker.

limits: Weights apply to the documented contract as a whole, not a measured size or severity of its remaining gap. Equal weights are ties, ordered by stable ID. Aggregate/acceptance/tooling contracts overlap capabilities: do not add weights into a completion percentage. Partially implemented earns no invented completion fraction. Completed critical contracts remain important but leave the unfinished queue. Scope changes need renewed review; new contracts stay unrated. Other engine tracks are not yet rated.
